claims.text: The target materials are as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi nanoscale thin films or patterned nanoribbons.
These films or nanoribbons have significant surface-to-volume ratios and inherent internal stress or disorder.
Surface and interface regions in low-dimensional FeMnNiGeSi increase magnetic anisotropy.
Increased magnetic anisotropy enhances domain-wall pinning.
Enhanced domain-wall pinning broadens magnetic hysteresis.
The nanoscale geometry limits heat dissipation across the films or nanoribbons.
Limited heat dissipation produces local nonequilibrium thermal gradients during rapid magnetic-cooling cycles.
Local nonequilibrium thermal gradients reduce the effective magnetocaloric entropy change.
A thin Cu or graphene capping layer will enhance heat transfer from the FeMnNiGeSi specimen.
Enhanced interfacial heat transfer from the capping layer will mitigate local thermal gradients during cycling.
Capped samples will show a larger magnetocaloric entropy change per field step than uncapped as-deposited controls.
Capped samples will show narrower hysteresis loops and lower hysteresis loss than uncapped controls.
Uncapped as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons have diminished magnetocaloric response because of poor heat dissipation.
Uncapped as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi films or nanoribbons have broadened hysteresis because of intrinsic surface pinning.
Magnetic entropy change is an appropriate metric for magnetocaloric performance.
Hysteretic losses can be important to the performance of magnetic-refrigeration materials.
The proposed mechanism applies at applied fields up to approximately 0.5 T, near the magnetic transition, and at cycling frequencies for which heat transfer limits performance.
The proposed mechanism is especially applicable to thicknesses from tens to a few hundred nanometers.
